authors.bio: Curtis Clark's credits include such artful narrative films as The Draughtsman's Contract, Dominick and Eugene, Alamo Bay, Extremities , and Talent for the Game. His extensive commercial cinematography projects have put him on the cutting edge, working for some of the industry's top directors and agencies. Clark currently heads the American Society of Cinematographers (ASC) Technology Committee, which examines and addresses imaging technology issues as they relate to the creation of motion pictures and cinematography. That committee worked closely with Digital Cinema Initiatives (DCI) to produce the ASC-DCI Standard Evaluation Material (StEM) used to evaluate the performance of digital projectors and other elements of digital cinema systems.
authors.name: Curtis Clark

authors.affiliation: Director of Media Systems at Pixar Animation Studios.
authors.bio: Howard Lukk is currently Director of Media Systems at Pixar Animation Studios. Before that, he was Vice President of Production Technology at The Walt Disney Studios, responsible for integrating new technology into feature film production and post-production. Lukk also worked as Director of Technology for DCI, where he researched and documented D-Cinema Specifications. He has also worked as a freelance engineer in the past, on HDTV productions such as Woodstock 25th Anniversary and Major League Baseball. Lukk is a SMPTE Fellow and has been an active member since 1995.
authors.name: Howard Lukk

authors.affiliation: Senior Vice President Technology and Operations for Deluxe Digital Cinema
authors.bio: Jim Whittlesey is senior Vice President Technology and Operations for Deluxe Digital Cinema. He was one of the first employees of the Deluxe Digital Cinema Division and helped build the organization into a worldwide leader for D-Cinema service, which includes mastering, content delivery, and security key management. Whittlesey worked for the Digital Cinema Initiatives (DCI) for three years and was responsible for editing the final version of the DCI Digital Cinema System Specification. While working at DCI, Whittlesey chaired the SMPTE AdHoc Digital Cinema Packaging group within DC28.20 Distribution Working Group. Whittlesey holds a B.S. degree in electrical engineering from Purdue University and an MBA from Portland State University. He is a member of SMPTE and participates in the D-Cinema groups.
authors.name: Jim Whittlesey
